- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) and prices are falling, model often underestimates the drop; increase forecast downward by 1–3% to align with true decline.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots in the following days; apply a “cool-down” correction: reduce forecast by 2–5% for 2–3 periods post-spike.
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67) and history shows mean reversion, model often fails to revert; adjust forecast toward historical mean over 10–15 day window.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently overestimates early in the horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is positive; apply a “lag correction” by subtracting 0.5–1.5% per day for first 7 days.
- When sentiment history shows repeated negative sentiment (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative values), model underreacts; increase forecast downward by 1–2% per negative sentiment day.
